title: Vendace, Marzipan and Kindziuk
lead: The cuisine of Warmia and Masuria is fish from the lakes, game, mushrooms, and Olsztyn marzipan. Rural flavors of the land of a thousand lakes. Slow travel through Warmian-Masurian cuisine.
body:
Why Warmian-Masurian cuisine, differently

The cuisine of Warmia and Masuria is the cuisine of the land of a thousand lakes — based on fish, game, and the gifts of the forest. Vendace, bream, pike, eel — all fish that have been finding their way to the tables of residents of this region for centuries, prepared in a variety of ways. Warmia and Masuria is a region where cuisine is still alive — based on local products, seasonal and deeply rooted in tradition.

Slow travel through Warmian-Masurian cuisine is a celebration of taste and tradition. Instead of rushing from restaurant to restaurant, stop in one longer — in a village inn, in a smokehouse by a lake, in an agritourism farm. Each dish has its own story, its own cook, its own lake. Ask where the fish comes from, how the dish is prepared, who passed down the recipe. This is a journey that rewards those who slow down — the longer you are in one place, the more flavors you can truly get to know.

What to see

Warmian-Masurian cuisine splits into several categories: lake fish (vendace, whitefish, eel, bream), game (boar, roe deer, red deer), mushroom dishes (dried, pickled, fried), baked goods (Olsztyn marzipan), cold cuts (kindziuk). Exploring the culinary region of Warmia and Masuria takes 2–3 days.

Lake fish

  • Smoked vendace — one of the most characteristic dishes of Warmia and Masuria. A delicate, fatty fish from Masurian lakes, smoked traditionally in home smokehouses. Worth trying by one of the Masurian lakes.
  • Smoked whitefish — similar to vendace but larger. Smoked, served with bread and butter. Available at smokehouses by the lakes.
  • Smoked eel — expensive but with an exceptional flavor. If you see a smokehouse with eels by the road, it is usually worth stopping.
  • Bream in sour cream — bream from Masurian lakes, stewed in sour cream with onion and spices. A Warmian classic.
  • Stuffed pike — pike from Masurian lakes, stuffed with fish meat, onion, and spices. A festive version, available in restaurants in Olsztyn.

Game and mushrooms

  • Kindziuk — a cold cut characteristic of the region, a ripening sausage made from boar or pork meat, seasoned with garlic and marjoram. Served cold, as a snack or with bread.
  • Boar in mushroom sauce — roast or stewed boar with mushroom sauce. Served with dumplings or potatoes.
  • Roe deer with juniper — roast roe deer with juniper and herbs. Served with modra kapusta and dumplings.
  • Dried mushrooms — gathered in the forests of Warmia and Masuria, dried and used in cooking all year. Worth trying in soups and sauces.
  • Mushroom soup — soup from dried mushrooms with groats or noodles. Warms you on cold days.

Baked goods and other specialties

  • Olsztyn marzipan — the sweet icon of the region, handmade from almonds and sugar, formed into various shapes, sold in pastry shops and souvenir stores throughout Olsztyn. The tradition dates back to the 18th century.
  • Warmian kołocz — sweet yeast cake with streusel and various additions. Baked for weddings and family celebrations.
  • Warmian cheesecake — cheesecake with curd cheese, raisins, and orange peel. Available at pastry shops in Olsztyn.
  • Beer from local breweries — several craft breweries in the region (Browar Warmia, Browar Jurand).
  • Mead — a traditional regional drink, available in shops with local products.

When to go

  • April–June — the best time for slow travel. Fewer tourists, fresh seasonal fish, long days. Worth a walk around smokehouses.
  • July–September — season for fresh fish, fruit, mushrooms. Worth it for fish markets by the lakes.
  • September–October — season for mushrooms, game, vendace. September is a good time for mushroom picking in Masurian forests.
  • November–March — season for game, bigos, soups. Worth it for winter cuisine, especially during the holiday season.

Getting there

Warmian-Masurian cuisine is from the northeastern region of Poland — best to travel by car or train, connecting several towns in one trip.

  • By train: Olsztyn, Giżycko, Mikołajki, Ełk have railway stations, with connections from most Polish cities.
  • By car: ~2.5 hours from Warsaw (S8 and DK16), ~2 hours from Gdańsk (S7 and DK16), ~2.5 hours from Białystok (DK8 and DK16).
  • By bus: PKS and private operators serve most towns on the route.

How much time you need

A weekend (2 days) is the minimum — Olsztyn (Olsztyn marzipan, vendace, kindziuk) and surroundings.

Three days is realistic for a first visit. Olsztyn, Giżycko, Mikołajki, Mrągowo.

A week lets you explore the whole culinary region of Warmia and Masuria — all the most important dishes and places.

What to eat and where to sleep

Instead of restaurants, choose smokehouses and village inns. There, cooks prepare what they have known since childhood, and they do it best.

  • Smoked vendace — a Warmian-Masurian classic, available at smokehouses by the lakes.
  • Olsztyn marzipan — the sweet icon of the region, available at pastry shops in Olsztyn.
  • Kindziuk — a cold cut from game, available in local shops.
  • Smoked eel — a regional delicacy, available at smokehouses by the lakes.
  • Mushroom soup — soup from dried mushrooms, available in local restaurants.
  • Beer from local breweries — several craft breweries in the region.

Accommodation: Olsztyn (largest choice, more options), Giżycko (town, more options), Mikołajki (resort, more options), Mrągowo (small town, smaller choice), agritourism farms in villages (quiet, home-cooked food).

Practical tips

  • Smokehouses — usually open from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m., longer in season. Check hours before your trip.
  • Regional restaurants — look for places where cooks prepare traditional recipes. Avoid tourist restaurants in city centres.
  • Culinary workshops — many farms and agritourism businesses offer workshops (smoking fish, baking bread, making marzipan). Book ahead.
  • Diet — Warmian-Masurian cuisine can be heavy and filling. Eat smaller portions to try more dishes.
  • Fish markets — the best place to buy fresh fish. Held regularly in Olsztyn and Giżycko.
  • Weather — weather in the region can be changeable. Even in July, bring a rain jacket.
  • Signal — good in towns, weaker in villages. Have an offline map.
tip: Buy Olsztyn marzipan at one of the traditional pastry shops in Olsztyn. It is the most authentic souvenir from the region, and its taste is incomparable to store-bought marzipan.
